quests.title: Hide five kind notes for people to find
quests.why: A kind note can turn someone’s whole day around.
steps: Five small bits of paper.
One kind line on each, for a different person.
Hide them where they’ll turn up tonight.

quests.title: Invent a game and teach it to someone
quests.why: Making the rules is the fun part.
steps: Pick three things you already have.
Make up the rules and a way to win.
Teach it and play one full round.

quests.title: Move for ten minutes, then see how you feel
quests.why: A low mood often lifts once your body warms up.
steps: Anything counts: dance, jump, run on the spot.
Ten minutes, no stopping.
Then tell Moss how you feel now.

quests.title: Build the best den you can, then read in it
quests.why: A den is a whole new room.
steps: Blankets, chairs, cushions.
Make a door and a light.
Read inside it for ten minutes.

quests.title: Build a cushion course and beat your own time
quests.why: Fizzy energy wants somewhere to go.
steps: Cushions, a chair, a rug.
Run it once to learn it.
Three more goes. Beat your first time.

quests.title: Twenty star jumps, ten hops, one lap of the house
quests.why: Use the fizz before it uses you.
steps: Clear a space.
Star jumps, hops, then the lap.
Flop on the floor and breathe.

quests.title: Put how you feel into a drawing, a song or a dance
quests.why: A feeling with somewhere to go gets lighter.
steps: Choose how: draw it, sing it or move it.
Make it as big as the feeling.
Show someone, or keep it for you.

quests.title: Make a cosy corner and read in it
quests.why: Sometimes the kindest thing is a blanket.
steps: Pillows, a blanket, one good book.
Fifteen minutes. Nobody disturbs you.
Tell a grown-up one line you liked.

quests.title: Squeeze, hold, let go. Five times.
quests.why: Big feelings pass faster when your body lets go first.
steps: Squeeze your fists, scrunch your face.
Hold for three. Let it all go.
Five times, then say one word for how you feel.

quests.title: Tell a grown-up how you feel, in one word
quests.why: Saying a feeling out loud makes it smaller.
steps: Find a grown-up you like talking to.
Pick one word for how you feel: tired, cross, worried, sad or happy.
Say your word to them. A hug is there if you want one.

quests.title: Run or scoot round the park three times
quests.why: Your legs have been sitting all day.
steps: Grown-up along, shoes on.
Three laps, any speed.
Stretch at the end.

quests.title: Make an instrument out of junk and play a tune
quests.why: Everything makes a sound if you ask it.
steps: Boxes, tins, rubber bands, rice.
Build one thing that makes a noise.
Play a tune someone can guess.

quests.title: At snack time, stop and ask: hungry or bored?
quests.why: Your body tells you what it needs, if you listen.
steps: Before the snack, stop for ten seconds.
Tummy rumbling, or nothing to do?
Say which out loud, then choose.

quests.title: Make a grown-up a drink without being asked
quests.why: The best kind things are the unasked ones.
steps: Notice who looks like they need one.
A cold one, the way they like it: water, squash or milk.
Hand it over. No need to say why.

quests.title: Find the sugar on a snack label and count it in spoons
quests.why: Four grams is one teaspoon. Now you’ll always know.
steps: Find ‘sugars’ on the back of a packet.
Divide by four. That’s your spoons.
Would you still pick it? Say why.

quests.title: Cook tea together: one chef, one sous-chef
quests.why: Two cooks, one kitchen, one plan.
steps: Pick the meal with a grown-up.
Chef decides, sous-chef preps. A grown-up does anything on the hob.
Find the protein, the carb and the veg.

quests.title: Tidy race: first to clear their bedroom floor wins
quests.why: A clear floor is a clear head. And bragging rights.
steps: A grown-up says go.
Everything off the floor, into its home.
Shout done. A grown-up checks both rooms.

quests.title: Water, a snack, then ten quiet minutes
quests.why: A tired brain after school is often a thirsty, hungry one.
steps: A big glass of water first.
A snack a grown-up is happy for you to have.
Ten quiet minutes: lie down, look outside or listen to music.

quests.title: Sit close to someone you like for five minutes
quests.why: Sad feels smaller when someone’s next to you.
steps: Pick your person: a grown-up, a brother or sister, or a pet.
Sit close for five minutes. A hug counts.
If you want, tell them one thing about today.

quests.title: Three good things, told at lights out
quests.why: Your brain falls asleep on whatever you give it last.
steps: Wait until the light goes off, not before.
Tell a grown-up three good things from today.
Big or tiny. A good sandwich counts.

quests.title: Leaf hunt: ten different leaves, and name three
quests.why: Every tree signs its name on its leaves.
steps: Grown-up along, coat on.
Ten leaves, no two the same.
Name three. Guess first, then check.

quests.title: Make soup together from three orange things
quests.why: Autumn tastes better when you made it.
steps: Pick three orange things with a grown-up.
One washes and peels, one chops with the claw. A grown-up does the hob.
Serve it to everyone at the table.

quests.title: Build Moss a bridge strong enough to hold a mug
quests.why: Engineers test their ideas. So can you.
steps: Two piles of books with a gap between.
Build a bridge across with bricks.
Test it with a mug of water. If it sags, make it stronger.

quests.title: Build how today felt, then tell someone about it
quests.why: Sometimes hands say it better than words.
steps: Think of how today felt as a weather: sunny, cloudy, windy, rainy or stormy.
Pick bricks in that weather’s colours and build it.
Show someone and tell them one thing about it.

quests.title: Build blind: one of you describes, the other builds
quests.why: Clear words and good listening, both at once.
steps: Sit back to back with the same bricks.
One describes a build step by step. No peeking.
Compare the two. Swap and go again.

quests.title: Make the batter, set out the toppings and serve the family
quests.why: One day a year the whole kitchen gets a turn.
steps: Weigh and whisk the batter with a grown-up.
A grown-up cooks and flips them at the hob. You lay out plates and toppings.
Serve them. Lemon and sugar, or your favourite.

quests.title: Post a thank-you to someone who never gets one
quests.why: The bin crew, the lollipop person, the librarian. They’d love it.
steps: Think of someone who helps and rarely hears thanks.
Write or draw them a short note.
Give it or post it with a grown-up, or leave it where they’ll find it.

quests.title: Make your bed all by yourself
quests.why: A made bed makes the whole room look finished.
steps: Pull the covers straight up to the top.
Plump the pillow and sit your toys on it.
Stand back and smooth out the lumps.

quests.title: Make your bed five mornings in a row
quests.why: A habit is just the same small thing, again and again.
steps: Make it properly before you leave the room.
Do it again tomorrow, and the day after.
Miss a morning and the run starts again.

quests.title: Put every toy back where it lives
quests.why: Toys you can find are toys you can play with.
steps: Gather every toy that is out.
Put each one back in its home.
Check under the bed and the sofa.

quests.title: Set the table for dinner
quests.why: A laid table says dinner is for everyone.
steps: Ask how many people are eating.
Plates, cutlery, cups, one for each.
Add one nice touch: napkins, water, a flower.

quests.title: Clear and wipe the table after dinner
quests.why: The meal is not over until the table is clear.
steps: Clear the plates once everyone has finished.
Scrape and stack them by the sink.
Wipe the table until there are no crumbs.

quests.title: Sort the washing into colour piles
quests.why: Whites stay white when they wash with whites.
steps: Tip out the washing basket.
Make piles for whites, darks and colours.
Ask a grown-up to check one pile.

quests.title: Wash, dry and fold a whole load of washing
quests.why: One day you will run your own home. Start with one load.
steps: Load and set the machine with a grown-up the first time.
Hang it or dry it properly.
Fold every item and put it away.

quests.title: Water the plants every day this week
quests.why: Plants cannot ask. Someone has to notice.
steps: Find out which plants need water and how much.
Water them each day without a reminder.
Feel the soil first. Damp means leave it.

quests.title: Tidy your room without being asked
quests.why: Doing it before anyone asks is the part people notice.
steps: Start before anyone mentions it.
Floor first, then surfaces, then the bed.
Put one thing back that has been out for ages.

quests.title: Keep your room tidy three days running
quests.why: Keeping it tidy is easier than tidying it.
steps: Tidy it properly on day one.
Put things back as you go, each day.
Five minutes before bed to catch the strays.

quests.title: Make your own snack and clear up after
quests.why: Making it is half the job. Clearing up is the other half.
steps: Pick a snack a grown-up is happy for you to have.
Make it yourself, no knives unless you are allowed.
Wipe up and put everything back.

quests.title: Help cook a family meal from scratch
quests.why: Everyone should know how a real meal is made.
steps: Ask a grown-up which jobs are yours.
Wash, weigh and chop with them beside you. A grown-up does the hob.
Name the protein, the carb and the veg.

quests.title: Pack your own bag for a day out
quests.why: The person who packs it knows what is in it.
steps: Think about the day: weather, food, fun.
Pack it all yourself.
Ask a grown-up to check one thing.

quests.title: Do the washing up all by yourself
quests.why: A clear sink at the end of the night is a gift to the morning.
steps: Hot soapy water, glasses first, pans last.
Sharp knives one at a time, never left hidden in the water.
Put it all away and wipe the sink.

quests.title: Hoover two whole rooms properly
quests.why: Proper means the corners too.
steps: Pick up small things from the floor first.
Hoover both rooms, edges and under chairs.
Empty the bin if it is full.

quests.title: Take the bins out and sort the recycling
quests.why: Somebody always does this. Tonight it is you.
steps: Empty the bins into the right outside bin.
Sort the recycling into the right boxes.
Put a fresh bag in each bin.

quests.title: Sort out one messy drawer or shelf
quests.why: One sorted drawer makes the whole room feel calmer.
steps: Empty it out completely.
Bin the rubbish, move what lives elsewhere.
Put the rest back in an order that makes sense.

quests.title: Clean the windows or mirrors until they shine
quests.why: Shiny glass makes a room look twice as clean.
steps: Glass you can reach from the floor, and the cleaner a grown-up gives you.
Spray, wipe, then buff.
Keep going until there are no streaks.

quests.title: Help unpack the shopping and put it away
quests.why: Many hands, one quick job.
steps: Carry bags in without being asked.
Put each thing where it lives.
Fold the bags away.

quests.title: Match every sock in the sock mountain
quests.why: Somewhere in that pile, every sock has a partner.
steps: Tip out the whole sock pile.
Match every pair you can find.
Roll the pairs and put the odd ones aside.

quests.title: Help wash the car inside and out
quests.why: A clean car feels new for about a week.
steps: Help wash and rinse the outside.
Clear the rubbish from inside.
Wipe the seats and dashboard.

quests.title: Run your morning routine on your own for three days
quests.why: Nobody reminding you is the best kind of morning.
steps: Up, dressed, fed and ready with no reminders.
Do it again the next morning.
And the one after that.

quests.title: Change your own bed sheets
quests.why: Fresh sheets you put on yourself feel even better.
steps: Strip the old sheets off.
Fitted sheet first, then the duvet cover.
Old sheets into the wash basket.

quests.title: Clear out one cupboard and bag things to give away
quests.why: Things you do not use could be someone else's favourite.
steps: Take everything out of the cupboard.
Keep, give away or bin. Be honest.
Bag the give-away pile and put the rest back neatly.

quests.title: Give someone a big thank-you hug and say why
quests.why: A hug with a reason is the best kind.
steps: Pick the person you want to thank.
Give them a big hug.
Tell them exactly what the thank-you is for.

quests.title: Write or draw a thank-you note for a grown-up at home
quests.why: Grown-ups hardly ever get thanked for the everyday things.
steps: Think of one thing they do for you all the time.
Write or draw a thank-you for that one thing.
Leave it where they will find it.

quests.title: Give a grown-up fifteen minutes of total peace
quests.why: Quiet is a present you can give without spending anything.
steps: Tell them: the next fifteen minutes are yours.
Keep yourself busy without asking for anything.
Tell them when the time is up.

quests.title: Phone or visit a grandparent or older relative for a proper chat
quests.why: They think about you more than you know.
steps: Ring or visit, with a grown-up's help.
Ask them two questions about their week.
Really listen to the answers.

quests.title: Make a card for someone who needs cheering up
quests.why: A card says I thought about you, and that helps.
steps: Think of someone having a hard time.
Make a card with something kind inside.
Give it or post it with a grown-up.

quests.title: Help a neighbour with a small job
quests.why: A street where people help is a better street to live on.
steps: Ask a grown-up which neighbour could use a hand.
Offer, then do the job with a grown-up nearby.
Do it properly, even the boring bit.

quests.title: Fill a bag for the food bank with a grown-up
quests.why: Some families near you are short this week. You can help.
steps: Find out what the food bank needs most.
Choose and pack the items with a grown-up.
Drop it off together.

quests.title: Choose three toys or books to give to someone who needs them
quests.why: A toy you have finished with could be someone's new favourite.
steps: Pick three things you have really grown out of.
Check with a grown-up that they can go.
Wipe them clean and bag them up.

quests.title: Include someone who looked left out
quests.why: Being asked in can change someone's whole day.
steps: Spot someone on their own.
Ask them to join your game or chat.
Tell a grown-up about it later.

quests.title: Check on a friend who has been quiet lately
quests.why: Quiet can mean something is wrong. Asking costs nothing.
steps: Think of a friend you have not heard from.
Ask how they really are: in person, or a call or message if you’re allowed.
Listen. You do not have to fix anything.

quests.title: Pick up litter on a walk, gloves on
quests.why: The park looks after you. This is you looking after it.
steps: Gloves on, bag in hand, grown-up along.
Pick up litter, never anything sharp or glass.
Put the bag in a proper bin.

quests.title: Look after a pet all day: food, water, exercise
quests.why: Pets count on someone every single day.
steps: Find out what they need and when.
Do every feed and water yourself, and walks the way your grown-up says.
No reminders from anyone.

quests.title: Thank someone who helps your family, and mean it
quests.why: Thanks lands best when it names the thing.
steps: Think of someone who helps your family.
Go and thank them.
Say exactly what for.

quests.title: Do a secret good deed nobody finds out about
quests.why: Nobody knowing it was you is what makes it count.
steps: Notice something that would quietly help someone.
Do it when they are not looking.
Tell Moss, never them.

quests.title: Teach someone younger a skill you are good at
quests.why: Teaching something is the best way to really know it.
steps: Pick something you can do well.
Show them slowly, one step at a time.
Let them have a go. Cheer the tries.

quests.title: Carry the shopping for your grown-up, no moaning
quests.why: Heavy bags are lighter shared.
steps: Offer before they ask.
Carry it the whole way.
Not one moan. Not even a small one.

quests.title: Do a kind thing for a neighbour three days running
quests.why: Once is nice. Three days is you being a good neighbour.
steps: Choose a neighbour with a grown-up.
Do one kind thing for them today.
Another tomorrow, and the day after.

quests.title: Bake something and share it with a neighbour or friend
quests.why: Something home-made says you took the time.
steps: Bake something simple with a grown-up for the oven.
Wrap some up, with a note of what’s in it in case of allergies.
Hand it over with a grown-up: a neighbour, a friend or a helper.

quests.title: Say sorry properly for something you got wrong
quests.why: A proper sorry fixes more than you would think.
steps: Work out what you actually got wrong.
Say sorry for that, with no excuses.
Ask if there is anything you can do to help.

quests.title: Clear up a mess that was not yours, no complaining
quests.why: Everyone's home, everyone's mess, anyone's job.
steps: Find a mess that is not yours.
Clear it without pointing it out.
Say nothing about it after, either.

quests.title: Volunteer an hour for a club, charity or community group
quests.why: An hour of your time is worth more than you think.
steps: Find a group that needs help, with a grown-up.
Give them a full hour of real work.
Ask what they need next time.

quests.title: Write down three things you love about each person at home
quests.why: People rarely hear the good things out loud.
steps: Think properly about each person.
Write three true things for each one.
Read one out, or leave it for them.

quests.title: Do a job for whoever usually does it at home
quests.why: Noticing who does the jobs is the start of sharing them.
steps: Spot a job one person always does.
Do it before they get to it.
Do it the way they would.

quests.title: Do a secret kind favour for your brother or sister
quests.why: Nobody knowing it was you is what makes it count.
steps: Notice one thing that would make their day easier.
Do it without telling them.
Tell Moss, not them.

quests.title: Let your brother or sister choose first, all day
quests.why: Going second is kinder than it feels.
steps: Every choice today, they go first.
No sighing, no arguing.
A grown-up checks at bedtime.

quests.title: Teach your brother or sister something you are good at
quests.why: You know things they would love to know.
steps: Pick something you can do well.
Show them slowly and let them try.
Cheer the tries, not just the wins.

quests.title: Sort a squabble with words, not shouting
quests.why: Calm words fix it. Shouting just makes it louder.
steps: When it heats up, stop and take three slow breaths.
Say what you want in a normal voice.
Listen to what they want too.

quests.title: Play a game your brother or sister picked, happily
quests.why: Their game matters to them. That is enough.
steps: Let them choose the game.
Play it properly, all the way through.
Say one thing you enjoyed.

quests.title: Learn to tie your own shoelaces
quests.why: Once you can tie them, nobody has to do it for you again.
steps: Ask someone to show you, slowly.
Bunny ears or round the tree. Pick one way.
Practise until you can do both shoes.

quests.title: Do all your own zips and buttons
quests.why: Getting dressed on your own is a big step.
steps: Practise on your coat zip first.
Then the buttons, from the bottom up.
Get fully dressed with no help.

quests.title: Learn to tell the time on a clock face
quests.why: Then you will always know how long until tea.
steps: The short hand shows the hour, the long hand the minutes.
Read o'clock, then half past, then quarter past.
Tell a grown-up the time three times today.

quests.title: Learn or level up your bike riding
quests.why: A bike is freedom on two wheels.
steps: Helmet on, tyres checked, grown-up along, away from cars.
Pick one thing to get better at: starting, turning, stopping.
Practise it until it is better than when you began.

quests.title: Read a book and tell someone the story
quests.why: Telling a story back shows you really got it.
steps: Read the book all the way to the end.
Tell someone what happened, in your own words.
Say which bit you liked most.

quests.title: Read for twenty minutes, three days running
quests.why: Twenty minutes a day adds up to whole books.
steps: Twenty minutes with a book today.
Same again tomorrow.
And the day after.

quests.title: Learn to make your own lunch
quests.why: A lunch you made yourself tastes better. It just does.
steps: Choose a lunch you are allowed to make.
Make it start to finish.
Clear up after yourself.

quests.title: Learn to sew on a button
quests.why: A lost button is a two-minute fix once you know how.
steps: Watch a grown-up thread a needle, then do it yourself.
Stitch through the holes six times each way.
Knot it at the back so it holds.

quests.title: Make a piece of art for the fridge gallery
quests.why: Every fridge needs a gallery.
steps: Decide what you want to make.
Take your time and finish it.
Give it a title and put it up.

quests.title: Learn ten words in another language
quests.why: Ten words is enough to say hello to a new country.
steps: Choose a language and ten useful words.
Say them out loud until they stick.
Test yourself with a grown-up.

quests.title: Build something by following the instructions all the way
quests.why: Following steps in order is a real skill.
steps: Read or look through all the instructions first.
Build it step by step without skipping.
Check it against the picture at the end.

quests.title: Learn to tie a proper knot and show it off
quests.why: The right knot holds when it matters.
steps: Pick one knot: a reef knot, a bowline or a clove hitch.
Practise until you can tie it without looking.
Show someone and let them test it.

quests.title: Learn to touch-type or code a tiny game
quests.why: Making the computer do what you want is a superpower.
steps: Pick touch-typing or a simple coding site with a grown-up.
Practise until you can do something new.
Show someone what you made or your speed.

quests.title: Practise an instrument on four days this week
quests.why: Little and often beats one long go.
steps: Pick one bit to get better at.
Practise it properly, not just playing what you know.
Four days this week, any four.

quests.title: Write a short story or comic and read it aloud
quests.why: Your ideas deserve to be heard.
steps: Plan a beginning, a middle and an end.
Write or draw it.
Read it aloud to someone.

quests.title: Learn to spell ten tricky words
quests.why: Tricky words are only tricky until you know them.
steps: Pick ten words you often get wrong.
Look, cover, write, check.
Get a grown-up to test you.

quests.title: Learn to read a map and plan a route
quests.why: A map-reader never really gets lost.
steps: Learn what the symbols and the scale mean.
Pick two places you know.
Plan the best route between them.

quests.title: Lead a family walk with no help getting there
quests.why: Leading the way is a different job to following.
steps: Study the route before you set off.
Lead the walk. Nobody corrects you.
Get everyone there and back.

quests.title: Try a new craft or hobby and show your first go
quests.why: Every expert started with a wobbly first go.
steps: Pick something you have never tried.
Have a proper go, however it turns out.
Say one thing you would do differently next time.

quests.title: Learn a poem or song by heart and perform it
quests.why: Something you know by heart stays with you.
steps: Choose a poem or song you like.
Learn it a line at a time.
Perform it for someone.

quests.title: Learn basic first aid: cuts, bumps and when to call for help
quests.why: Knowing what to do keeps you calm when it matters.
steps: Learn how to clean and cover a small cut.
Learn what to do for a bump or a burn.
Learn when to call the emergency number, and what to say.

quests.title: Learn to use the hob safely, with a grown-up
quests.why: Heat is a tool. Learn to use it properly.
steps: Learn the safety rules from a grown-up first.
Cook something simple with them watching the whole time.
Turn everything off and check it twice.

quests.title: Learn five facts about something new and teach someone
quests.why: The best way to remember something is to teach it.
steps: Pick something you know nothing about.
Find five facts with a grown-up's help.
Teach them to someone at tea.

quests.title: Get yourself ready on time, no reminders, three days
quests.why: No nagging is a nice way to start the day, for everyone.
steps: Know what time you need to be ready.
Get there without anyone reminding you.
Three mornings in a row.

quests.title: Invent a dance and teach it to the family
quests.why: A dance you made up belongs to you.
steps: Pick a song you love.
Make up four moves and put them in order.
Teach it to the family and dance it together.

quests.title: Practise one sport skill for thirty minutes
quests.why: Thirty minutes on one thing beats an hour on everything.
steps: Pick one skill: kicking, catching, shooting, serving.
Warm up, then practise just that.
Count your best go at the end.

quests.title: Move your body every morning for five days
quests.why: Moving first thing wakes your brain up too.
steps: Pick your morning move: stretches, jumps, a quick jog.
Five minutes, before breakfast.
Five mornings in a row.

quests.title: Go on a family walk adventure
quests.why: Walks are where the best chats happen.
steps: Plan a route with your family.
Walk the whole way, no moaning.
Spot three things you have never noticed before.

quests.title: Swim or splash for a whole session
quests.why: Water makes your whole body work, and it feels like play.
steps: Get to the pool with a grown-up. If you’re under 8, they swim with you.
Swim, splash or practise for the whole session.
Try one thing you could not do last time.

quests.title: Play outside for a whole hour, no screens
quests.why: Outside is the biggest playroom there is.
steps: Leave every screen indoors.
Play outside for a full hour, somewhere your grown-up says is OK.
Come in with muddy knees if you can.

quests.title: Learn a new skipping or ball trick
quests.why: Tricks are just practice you can show off.
steps: Choose a trick you cannot do yet.
Break it into small bits and practise each one.
Keep going until you land it three times.

quests.title: Try a sport or activity you have never done
quests.why: You might find your new favourite thing.
steps: Pick something new: a club, a class, or a game in the park with a grown-up.
Give it a proper go, even if it feels odd at first.
Say one thing you liked.

quests.title: Plan and lead a family workout
quests.why: Leading is harder than joining in. Try it.
steps: Plan six moves everyone can do.
Warm everyone up, then run the workout.
Cool down together at the end.

quests.title: Plan a bike or scooter route and ride it with a grown-up
quests.why: A route you planned feels like your own adventure.
steps: Plan a new route on a map with a grown-up.
Helmets on, brakes checked, lights if you need them.
Ride it together, the whole way.

quests.title: Do fifteen minutes of yoga or stretching
quests.why: Stretching tells your body it can slow down.
steps: Find a yoga video with a grown-up, or a stretching card.
Follow it for fifteen minutes, slowly.
Lie still and breathe at the end.

quests.title: Get the whole family playing a game outside
quests.why: Everyone moving together is the best kind of noise.
steps: Choose a game everyone can play.
Round everyone up. Yes, everyone.
Play until someone wins.

quests.title: Hit 10,000 steps in one day
quests.why: Steps add up faster than you think, once you start counting.
steps: Work out how you will count your steps.
Walk more on purpose: stairs, a family walk, the long way round.
Keep going until you pass 10,000.

quests.title: Climb, balance and explore at the park for an hour
quests.why: Climbing makes you stronger and braver at the same time.
steps: Get to the park with a grown-up.
Climb, balance, swing and explore.
Try one thing that felt tricky last time, with your grown-up close.

quests.title: Beat your own record at something physical
quests.why: The only person to beat is yesterday's you.
steps: Pick something you can measure: keepy-uppies, a sprint, a plank.
Do your best and write it down.
Rest, then try to beat it.

quests.title: Walk somewhere together instead of getting a lift
quests.why: You notice more on foot than from a car seat.
steps: Choose a trip you would normally be driven.
Plan the route with a grown-up.
Walk it together, the whole way.

quests.title: Train one skill on four days and show the progress
quests.why: Proof that practice works is the best motivation there is.
steps: Pick one skill and measure where you start.
Train it on four days this week.
Measure again and compare.

quests.title: Take five big belly breaths when you feel wobbly
quests.why: Slow breaths tell your body it is safe.
steps: Sit or lie somewhere comfy.
Hand on your tummy. Breathe in and feel it rise.
Five slow ones, then tell a grown-up how you feel.

quests.title: Name how you feel with a feelings word
quests.why: A feeling with a name is easier to handle.
steps: Stop and notice what is going on inside.
Pick a word: cross, sad, worried, excited, fed up.
Tell a grown-up your word.

quests.title: Draw or write three things you are grateful for
quests.why: Looking for good things helps you find more of them.
steps: Think back over your day or week.
Draw or write three things you are glad about.
Put it somewhere you will see it.

quests.title: Make a thankful list before bed, three nights
quests.why: Ending the day on good things helps you sleep.
steps: In bed, think of three good things from today.
Write them down or say them to a grown-up.
Do it again for the next two nights.

quests.title: Have a whole afternoon with no screens
quests.why: A screen-free afternoon is longer than you think, in a good way.
steps: Agree the time with a grown-up.
Screens off and out of sight.
Fill it with anything else: build, read, go out, make.

quests.title: Take a slow ten-minute noticing walk
quests.why: Walking slowly lets you see what rushing misses.
steps: Walk somewhere quiet with a grown-up.
Go slowly. Notice sounds, smells and colours.
Name five things you noticed.

quests.title: Lights out on time three nights running
quests.why: Sleep is when your body and brain get stronger.
steps: Know your lights-out time.
Be in bed, ready, before it.
Three nights in a row.

quests.title: Say three kind things about yourself out loud
quests.why: You deserve the kind words you give other people.
steps: Stand somewhere you feel comfy.
Say three true, kind things about yourself.
Pick one to remember tomorrow.

quests.title: Use five slow breaths instead of shouting, three times
quests.why: The pause before you shout is where you get to choose.
steps: Catch the moment just before you shout.
Take five slow breaths instead.
Tell a grown-up each time you manage it.

quests.title: Keep a worry journal for three days
quests.why: Worries on paper are smaller than worries in your head.
steps: Write down what is worrying you, for five minutes.
Under each one, write one thing you could do about it.
Do it again the next two days.

quests.title: Tell a grown-up about something on your mind
quests.why: Worries shrink when someone else helps you hold them.
steps: Choose a grown-up you trust.
Pick a calm moment, like a walk or bedtime.
Tell them what has been on your mind.

quests.title: Wait calmly for something you really want
quests.why: Waiting is hard. Getting better at it is worth it.
steps: Notice that you want it right now.
Find something else to do while you wait.
No nagging, no sulking.

quests.title: Have fifteen minutes of quiet time on your own
quests.why: Quiet time fills your batteries back up.
steps: Find a spot where nobody will disturb you.
No screens. Read, draw, look out of the window.
Notice how you feel after.

quests.title: Try the 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 senses calming trick
quests.why: Your senses can pull you back into the room.
steps: Name five things you can see and four you can touch.
Then three you can hear, two you can smell, one you can taste.
Tell a grown-up how you feel now.

quests.title: Fix a falling-out by listening first
quests.why: People calm down faster when they feel heard.
steps: Wait until you both feel calmer.
Let them talk first. Listen properly.
Then say your side, and agree one thing.

quests.title: Put screens away an hour before bed, three nights
quests.why: An hour with no screens helps your brain get ready for sleep.
steps: Pick your screens-away time.
Put them in another room, not just face down.
Three nights running.

quests.title: Try something you might not be good at yet
quests.why: Not good at it yet is how everything starts.
steps: Pick something you think you might be bad at.
Try it anyway.
Keep going past the awkward bit.

quests.title: Catch an unkind thought about yourself and swap it
quests.why: You would not talk to a friend like that. So do not talk to yourself like that.
steps: Notice a harsh thought about yourself.
Ask: is it true, or just loud?
Swap it for something truer and kinder.

quests.title: Do your whole wind-down routine on your own
quests.why: A calm routine tells your body sleep is coming.
steps: Bath or wash, teeth, pyjamas.
Every step without being told.
Into bed with a book.

quests.title: Sort a coin jar into piles and name each coin
quests.why: Knowing your coins is the first money skill.
steps: Tip the coins out onto a tray.
Make a pile for each kind of coin.
Say the name of each pile out loud.

quests.title: Count a pile of coins and write down the total
quests.why: Counting money carefully means you always know what you have.
steps: Sort the coins into piles first.
Count each pile, then add them up.
Write the total and check it once more.

quests.title: Make a needs and wants list
quests.why: Needs come first. Wants are the fun extras.
steps: Draw two columns: needs and wants.
Put at least five things in each.
Circle the one want you would save for.

quests.title: Save some pocket money instead of spending it
quests.why: Money you keep today can become something bigger later.
steps: Decide how much you will save before you spend.
Put it somewhere safe, away from your spending money.
Leave it there all week.

quests.title: Set a savings goal and make a picture chart
quests.why: Seeing how close you are makes saving easier.
steps: Choose something real to save for.
Draw a chart with one box for each bit you save.
Colour in the first box.

quests.title: Compare the price of one thing in two shops
quests.why: The same thing can cost very different amounts.
steps: Pick one thing you actually want.
Check its price in two shops, or two websites with a grown-up.
Work out the difference and where you would buy it.

quests.title: Write down every bit of money you spend for three days
quests.why: You cannot manage money you do not notice.
steps: Keep a note in your pocket or on a phone.
Write down every spend, however small.
Add it up at the end of day three.

quests.title: Earn a bonus doing an extra job at home
quests.why: Money you earn feels different to money you are given.
steps: Agree an extra job and the pay with a grown-up.
Do it properly, to their standard.
Decide what to do with what you earned.

quests.title: Want something? Wait a day, then decide
quests.why: If you still want it tomorrow, it is probably worth it.
steps: When you want something, write it down.
Wait a whole day before asking.
Decide: still want it, or not?

quests.title: Help plan a food shop and keep it under budget
quests.why: Every family budget is really just a list and a number.
steps: Agree a budget with a grown-up.
Plan the list and price it up.
Help choose swaps to stay under.

quests.title: Buy or make a gift for someone on a small budget
quests.why: A small budget makes you think harder about what they would love.
steps: Set your budget before you look.
Make it, or buy it with a grown-up, within budget.
Wrap it and give it.

quests.title: Learn what a bank account and interest are
quests.why: Interest is money that grows while you are not looking.
steps: Ask a grown-up to explain accounts and interest.
Look up one real savings rate together.
Work out what it would add to {100} in a year.

quests.title: Sell or give away something you no longer use
quests.why: Things you do not use are worth more to someone else.
steps: Choose something you really do not use.
Decide: sell it or give it away.
Do it with a grown-up. They handle any selling online.

quests.title: Read a receipt and check every line
quests.why: Shops make mistakes too. Checking is smart.
steps: Get a receipt from a real shop.
Check each item and price.
Add it up and see if the total matches.

quests.title: Split your pocket money into save, spend and give
quests.why: Three jars, three jobs. Every bit of money has a plan.
steps: Get three jars or envelopes.
Label them save, spend and give.
Split your money between them.

quests.title: Find the best-value snack in the shop and explain why
quests.why: Cheapest is not always best value.
steps: In a shop with a grown-up, compare three snacks by price and size.
Work out which gives you the most for the money.
Explain your pick to a grown-up.

quests.title: Work out what a subscription really costs a year
quests.why: Small monthly amounts hide big yearly ones.
steps: Find the monthly price of one subscription.
Times it by twelve.
Decide if it is worth that much.

quests.title: Run a mini stall or car wash for people you know
quests.why: Running a stall teaches you more about money than any lesson.
steps: Plan it with a grown-up: what, where, what price.
Run it with a grown-up there the whole time.
Count the takings and take away what it cost.

quests.title: Go five days without asking to buy anything
quests.why: Not asking is harder than it sounds. That is the point.
steps: No asking to buy anything, for anything.
Write wants on a list instead.
Look at the list on day five.

quests.title: Run a shop at home with real coins and give change
quests.why: Playing shops is how real shopkeepers learned.
steps: Set up a shop with prices on everything.
Sell to the family with real coins, and give the right change.
Count your takings at closing time.

quests.title: Find out what three things at home cost
quests.why: Everything at home was bought by someone.
steps: Choose three everyday things: milk, bread, soap.
Ask a grown-up or look at the receipt.
Put them in order, cheapest first.

quests.title: Choose the cheaper of two treats and say why
quests.why: Choosing is a skill. Practise on something tasty.
steps: With a grown-up, look at two treats and their prices.
Choose the cheaper one.
Say why it is still a good pick.

quests.title: Add to your savings jar three days running
quests.why: Little bits every day make a full jar.
steps: Find a coin or two to save today.
Drop them in your jar.
Do it again tomorrow, and the day after.

quests.title: Plan a family treat that costs nothing at all
quests.why: The best treats are often free.
steps: Think of a treat that costs nothing: a picnic, a walk, a show.
Plan when and what everyone needs.
Ask the family if they are in.

quests.title: Invent a new sandwich and name it after yourself
quests.why: Every famous sandwich was someone's idea once.
steps: Find what you are allowed to use.
Build a sandwich nobody has made before.
Name it, then eat the evidence.

quests.title: Put a song on and tidy one room before it ends
quests.why: Tidying is quicker with a beat.
steps: Pick one room and a loud song.
Tidy as much as you can before it ends.
Freeze when the music stops.

quests.title: Make someone breakfast in bed
quests.why: Breakfast in bed makes anyone feel like a king or queen.
steps: Find out what they like for breakfast.
Make it, with a grown-up for anything hot.
Carry the tray to them carefully.

quests.title: Grow something from a seed and keep it alive all week
quests.why: Watching something grow because of you is a little bit of magic.
steps: Plant a seed or a bean in soil.
Check it and water it every day.
Look for the first green bit.

quests.title: Redesign one corner of your room
quests.why: Your space should feel like yours.
steps: Pick one corner and decide how it should feel.
Snap it before you start, then clear and rearrange.
Show a grown-up the before and after.

quests.title: Run the kitchen for one meal: choose it, cook it, serve it
quests.why: Head chef for a night. Everyone eats what you decide.
steps: Choose the meal and check the ingredients are in.
Cook it yourself, a grown-up nearby for anything hot.
Serve it and take the compliments.

quests.title: Put on a sock puppet show, then match the whole pile
quests.why: Odd socks make the best actors.
steps: Turn odd socks into puppets.
Put on a short show for someone.
Then match every sock left in the pile.

quests.title: Put on a show for the family: magic, jokes, dancing, anything
quests.why: Everyone loves a show, especially one made at home.
steps: Choose your act.
Practise it twice.
Perform it properly, with a bow at the end.

quests.title: Plan a surprise for someone on a completely ordinary day
quests.why: Surprises on ordinary days are the ones people remember.
steps: Pick someone and think what would delight them.
Set it up in secret.
Let them find it.

quests.title: Make a bird feeder and hang it where you can watch it
quests.why: Birds get hungry too, especially when it is cold.
steps: Make a feeder from a bottle, a pine cone or a card tube.
Fill it with seed from November to April, or fat balls from May to October.
Hang it where you can see it from a window. A grown-up does anything high.

quests.title: Catch someone being kind and tell them why it mattered
quests.why: Kindness grows when someone notices it.
steps: Watch out for someone doing something kind.
Tell them exactly what you saw.
Say why it mattered.

quests.title: Make a present from things you already have
quests.why: Made-by-you beats bought, every time.
steps: Choose who it is for and what they would like.
Make it only from things already in the house.
Wrap it, or hide it for them to find.

quests.title: Teach a grown-up a game you love and play it properly
quests.why: Grown-ups need teaching sometimes too.
steps: Pick a game you know really well.
Explain the rules clearly.
Play a full round together.

quests.title: Learn a magic trick and fool somebody with it
quests.why: A good trick needs practice nobody ever sees.
steps: Find a trick you can learn today.
Practise until it works every time.
Perform it and never tell the secret.

quests.title: Film and edit a one-minute video about something you love
quests.why: Making something is more fun than watching it.
steps: Pick your subject and plan what happens.
Film your clips, no faces needed.
Cut it to one minute exactly. It’s for the family, not for posting.

quests.title: Do a kitchen science experiment and explain what happened
quests.why: Science is just asking what happens if.
steps: Choose a safe experiment with a grown-up.
Guess what will happen, then run it.
Explain what really happened.

quests.title: Draw a treasure map and send someone on the hunt
quests.why: X marks the spot. You decide where.
steps: Draw your house or garden with the landmarks.
Hide something and mark it with an X.
Send someone on the hunt.

quests.title: Become the family expert on one odd topic and give a two-minute talk
quests.why: Everyone should be the expert on something.
steps: Pick a topic nobody at home knows about.
Find out enough to talk for two minutes.
Give your talk at tea.

quests.title: Learn to cook one dish from another country
quests.why: Food is the tastiest way to travel.
steps: Choose a country and a dish you can make.
Make it with a grown-up nearby. A grown-up does anything on the hob.
Tell everyone one thing about where it comes from.

quests.title: Learn a new game with real rules and teach it to someone
quests.why: Knowing the rules properly makes you the best person to play with.
steps: Choose a card, board or playground game.
Learn the rules until you can explain them.
Teach someone and play a round.

quests.title: Have a proper water fight outside
quests.why: Some days are made for getting soaked.
steps: Check with a grown-up and get outside.
Fill the bottles, buckets or balloons.
Have the water fight. Commit to it.

quests.title: Climb something outdoors you have never climbed before
quests.why: The view from somewhere new is always worth it.
steps: Find something safe and new: a climbing frame, a low tree, a big rock.
A grown-up spots you. No higher than they can reach.
Climb it, then climb down slowly.

quests.title: Build the biggest outdoor den or sandcastle you can
quests.why: Big builds need big ideas.
steps: Gather sticks, sand, boxes or blankets, with a grown-up close by.
Build it as big as you can manage.
Give it a name.

quests.title: Walk to see a sunrise or sunset from somewhere high
quests.why: The sky puts on a show twice a day. Go and watch one.
steps: Check when the sun rises or sets.
Walk somewhere with a view, with a grown-up.
Be there in time and watch it all.

quests.title: Learn a whole dance routine and perform it
quests.why: Learning a routine trains your memory and your legs.
steps: Choose a routine and learn it bit by bit.
Practise until you can do the whole thing.
Perform it for someone.

quests.title: Go barefoot on grass or sand and say how it feels
quests.why: Your feet have a lot to tell you.
steps: Find soft grass or sand a grown-up has checked, and take your shoes off.
Walk around slowly.
Tell someone three words for how it feels.

quests.title: Lie on your back and find five shapes in the clouds
quests.why: Clouds are the slowest show on earth.
steps: Find a comfy spot outside, where your grown-up says is OK, and lie back.
Watch the clouds drift.
Find five shapes and tell someone.

quests.title: Make one playlist that matches your mood and one that changes it
quests.why: Music can meet you where you are, then take you somewhere better.
steps: Make a playlist that sounds like how you feel now.
Make a second one that lifts you somewhere better.
Play the second one all the way through.

quests.title: Make three different people properly laugh
quests.why: Laughing is catching. Start it.
steps: Think what makes each person laugh.
Jokes, faces, a silly walk, anything.
Three different people, three real laughs.

quests.title: Sleep somewhere different in the house for one night
quests.why: The same house feels new from a different spot.
steps: Pick your spot with a grown-up: the floor, a den, the sofa.
Set it up cosy.
Sleep there all night.

quests.title: Make a calm box with five things that help when you feel wobbly
quests.why: When you feel wobbly, you will know exactly where to look.
steps: Find a box.
Add five things: something to hold, smell, look at, read and do.
Keep it somewhere you can reach.

quests.title: Look at the stars for ten minutes with a grown-up
quests.why: Looking at stars makes worries feel smaller.
steps: Wait for a clear night and ask a grown-up to come out with you.
Garden, doorstep or open window, lights off. Let your eyes adjust.
Ten minutes of looking up.

quests.title: Plan and have the most relaxing hour you can think of
quests.why: Knowing how to properly relax is a real skill.
steps: Plan the hour: what, where, what gets switched off.
Set it up.
Do it, with no interruptions.

quests.title: Rank three ice creams for taste and price and crown a winner
quests.why: The best ice cream is not always the priciest.
steps: Pick three ice creams and note each price.
Score each for taste, then for value.
Crown the winner.

quests.title: Plan the best day out you can for {10} and pitch it
quests.why: A small budget makes for a cleverer plan.
steps: Work out what {10} has to cover: travel, food, the thing itself.
Plan the whole day inside the budget.
Pitch it to the family.

quests.title: Hunt the whole house for forgotten coins and count them
quests.why: There is often money down the back of the sofa.
steps: Hunt sofas, cushions and coat pockets you’re allowed to check.
Sort what you find into piles.
Count the total and show a grown-up.

quests.title: Make something by hand and work out what you would charge
quests.why: Your time is worth something too.
steps: Make something properly by hand.
Add up what the materials cost.
Decide a price that covers your time too.

quests.title: Run a cinema night at home on a {10} budget
quests.why: Home cinema, same fun, much cheaper.
steps: Find out what a real cinema trip would cost.
Plan the film, snacks and seats for under {10}.
Make tickets and run the night.

quests.title: Take {5} and make the whole family a pudding
quests.why: Stretching a small amount is a real skill.
steps: Find a pudding that feeds everyone for {5}.
Shop for it with a grown-up and keep the receipt.
Make it, with a grown-up for the oven.

quests.title: Design your dream shop and work out what it would cost to open
quests.why: Every shop you walk past had to add all this up.
steps: Decide what your shop sells and who it is for.
List the real costs: rent, stock, staff, signs.
Add it up and decide what you would charge.

quests.title: Team blitz: tidy one room together
quests.why: Two people, half the time.
steps: Agree who does what before you start.
Both work until the whole room is done.
Check it together at the end.

quests.title: Invent an obstacle course and both finish it
quests.why: Design it together, cheer each other round.
steps: Design the course together, safely.
Both of you do the whole thing.
Time each other, then try to beat it.

quests.title: Cook or bake together, everyone with a job
quests.why: A kitchen works best when everyone has a job.
steps: Pick a recipe and share out the jobs.
Make it together. A grown-up does the oven and the hob.
Everyone helps clear up.

quests.title: Lead each other through five minutes of calm breathing
quests.why: Calm is easier when someone does it with you.
steps: Sit together somewhere quiet.
Take turns leading slow breaths.
Five minutes, then say one word each for how you feel.

quests.title: Run a pretend shop: one shopkeeper, one customer on a budget
quests.why: Shops are more fun with a real customer.
steps: Set up a shop with prices on everything.
One sells, one buys with a set budget.
Swap over.

quests.title: Plan and do a surprise nice thing for a grown-up
quests.why: Two heads make a better surprise.
steps: Plan the surprise together, in secret.
Both do a part of it.
Let them find it.

quests.title: Clean the car or garden as a team
quests.why: A big job shared is a big job done.
steps: Split the job into fair halves.
Both work until the whole thing is done.
Check each other's half.

quests.title: Build something big together from instructions
quests.why: One reads, one builds, then swap.
steps: Read the instructions together first.
Take turns reading and building.
Finish it and give it a place.

quests.title: Get outside together for a whole hour, nobody moans
quests.why: An hour outside together beats an hour inside apart.
steps: Agree where with a grown-up, and take one along.
Stay out for a full hour, all of you.
Not one moan the whole time.

quests.title: Sort a box for charity together
quests.why: Things you have outgrown can start again with someone else.
steps: Go through your things together.
Agree what goes in the box.
Check it with a grown-up.

quests.title: Set each other a treasure hunt and solve them both
quests.why: Your brain works differently when you are the one hiding it.
steps: Each hide something and write six clues to it.
Swap clues.
Solve each other's hunt.

quests.title: Invent a board game with real rules and play a full match
quests.why: Inventing rules together takes real teamwork.
steps: Decide what the game is about and how you win.
Make the board and pieces from paper.
Play a full match to the end.

quests.title: Write ten quiz questions each, then quiz each other
quests.why: Writing a good question is harder than answering one.
steps: Write ten questions each, in secret, with answers.
Take turns asking. One point each.
Add up the scores, no arguing.

quests.title: Skill swap: teach each other something for half an hour each
quests.why: You both know things the other one doesn't.
steps: Each pick something you are good at.
Teach yours for half an hour.
Swap over.

quests.title: Run a home Olympics with events, scores and medals
quests.why: Every champion started somewhere. Why not at home?
steps: Invent five events you can do safely.
Run them all and keep score.
Hold a medal ceremony.

quests.title: Learn a whole dance routine together and perform it
quests.why: Dancing in time with someone is harder and better.
steps: Pick a routine you can both learn.
Practise until you are in time.
Perform it for someone.

quests.title: Sort a shared shelf so it actually makes sense
quests.why: A shelf you both sorted is a shelf you can both find things on.
steps: Take everything off the shelf.
Agree an order that makes sense.
Put it all back that way.

quests.title: Build a reading den and read in it for an hour
quests.why: Reading side by side is quiet company.
steps: Build a den big enough for both of you.
Read in it for a whole hour.
Put everything back after.

quests.title: Make up a story together, one line each
quests.why: Nobody knows where it will end. That is the fun.
steps: One person starts with a single line.
Take turns adding a line.
Keep going until it has a proper ending.

quests.title: Make a scavenger hunt list and find it all outdoors
quests.why: Looking for things makes you notice everything.
steps: Write a list of twenty things to find outside.
Go and find them together, grown-up along.
Tick them all off.

quests.title: Learn a new card game properly and play best of five
quests.why: A new game learned together is yours to keep.
steps: Pick a card game neither of you knows.
Learn the rules properly.
Play best of five.

quests.title: Plan a whole film night: film, snacks, seats, tickets
quests.why: A film night you planned is better than one that just happens.
steps: Agree the film, snacks and start time.
Make tickets and set up the room.
Tear the tickets and enjoy it.

quests.title: Get everything ready for your first day back
quests.why: A ready bag makes the first morning easy.
steps: Find your bag, shoes and anything with your name on it.
Put it all in one place by the door.
Show a grown-up it is sorted.

quests.title: Give your room a proper end-of-Showdown reset
quests.why: A fresh start needs a fresh room.
steps: Everything off the floor and out from under the bed.
Three piles: keep, give away, throw away.
Put the keep pile back properly.

quests.title: Thank someone who made this Showdown good
quests.why: Someone helped you get here. Tell them.
steps: Think of one person who made this Showdown better.
Tell them exactly what they did.
Write it, draw it or say it to them.

quests.title: Do one secret good deed for every person in your house
quests.why: Everyone gets one. Nobody knows who did it.
steps: Count the people in your house.
Do one kind thing for each, without being seen.
At the end, see who noticed.

quests.title: Teach someone the best thing you learned
quests.why: Teaching it is how you know you really learned it.
steps: Pick the best thing you learned.
Break it into steps someone could follow.
Teach it, then let them try.

quests.title: Make the story of your Showdown
quests.why: You did a lot. Put it somewhere you can look back at.
steps: Choose your five best bits.
Put them in order, first to last.
Make them into a comic, a page or a poster.

quests.title: Beat your own record at something you have practised
quests.why: You have been practising. Time to see it.
steps: Pick something you have got better at.
Find your best score so far.
Warm up, then try to beat it.

quests.title: Lead one last big outdoor adventure
quests.why: Finish the Showdown the way you started it: outside.
steps: Decide where and what, with a grown-up.
Tell the family the plan.
Lead the whole thing.

quests.title: Name three things you are proud of
quests.why: Proud is a good feeling to finish on.
steps: Think back over the whole Showdown.
Find three things you are proud of.
Tell them to someone.

quests.title: Pick one thing you want to be better at this year
quests.why: A goal you choose is one you will actually chase.
steps: Think of one thing you found hard.
Turn it into something you can practise.
Write the first small step and when.

quests.title: Make your plan for the first morning back
quests.why: A calm first morning starts the night before.
steps: Work out when you need to be up and out.
Write the order you will do things in.
Put the list where you will see it.

quests.title: Count what you saved and give it a job
quests.why: Money with a job does not disappear.
steps: Gather everything you have saved.
Count it and write the total.
Decide its job: save, spend or give. Say why.

quests.title: Spend a little of your own money on someone else
quests.why: Spending on someone else feels surprisingly good.
steps: Think of someone who would love a small surprise.
Work out what you can afford.
Make it, or get it with a grown-up, and give it.

quests.title: Count your coins and pick one thing to save for
quests.why: Knowing what you have is step one.
steps: Tip out your coins and sort them.
Count each pile with a grown-up.
Pick one thing to save for.

quests.title: Keep a spend and save diary for three days
quests.why: Writing it down is how you find out where money goes.
steps: Write down everything you spend and save today.
Same again tomorrow.
On day three, add it all up.

quests.title: Wait calmly all day, without complaining
quests.why: Waiting gets easier every time you practise it.
steps: Notice each time you have to wait today.
Take a slow breath instead of moaning.
A grown-up checks in at bedtime.

quests.title: Order your own food and say thank you
quests.why: Your voice works. This is how you find out.
steps: At a café with a grown-up, decide what you want before you order.
Say it clearly yourself.
Say thank you when it arrives.

quests.title: Show the family something you made and explain it
quests.why: Talking about your own work is a skill worth having.
steps: Choose something you made and are proud of.
Show the family.
Explain how you made it and what was hardest.

quests.title: Try something brand new you have never done
quests.why: Brave is doing it while it still feels strange.
steps: Pick something you have really never done.
Do it, even though it feels unfamiliar.
Tell someone how it went.

quests.title: Read a story aloud to someone
quests.why: Stories are better out loud.
steps: Choose a story you enjoy.
Read it to someone, with voices if you like.
Ask them their favourite bit.

quests.title: Thank three people today and tell them exactly why
quests.why: A thank-you with a reason is one people keep.
steps: Think of three people who help you.
Thank each one.
Say exactly what for.

quests.title: Swap thirty minutes of screen time for outdoor play
quests.why: Outside charges you up. Screens run you down.
steps: Pick thirty minutes you would normally be on a screen.
Go outside instead, somewhere a grown-up says is OK.
Play anything you like.

quests.title: Have a screen-free morning
quests.why: A morning without screens feels longer, in a good way.
steps: No screens from the moment you wake.
Fill the morning with something else.
Tell a grown-up what you did instead.

quests.title: Say please and thank you every time today, no reminders
quests.why: Please and thank you make people glad to help you.
steps: Every ask gets a please.
Everything you are given gets a thank you.
A grown-up counts the reminders. Zero wins.

quests.title: Let people finish talking before you speak, all day
quests.why: Everyone likes being listened to all the way to the end.
steps: Wait until they have finished talking.
Count one in your head, then talk.
Ask a grown-up at bedtime how you did.

quests.title: Greet everyone you meet today by name
quests.why: Hearing your own name said kindly is a nice start to anything.
steps: Look up from what you are doing.
Say hello and their name.
Count how many people you greeted.

quests.title: Do a job the first time you are asked, no sighing
quests.why: Doing it straight away is quicker than arguing about it.
steps: Listen to what you are asked to do.
Say OK and start within a minute.
Finish it before doing anything else.

quests.title: Ask a grown-up for three no's today, and take each one calmly
quests.why: Hearing no calmly gets easier with practice.
steps: Tell a grown-up: give me three no's today.
Each time, breathe once and say OK.
Three calm OKs and you are done.

quests.title: Argue your side of something politely for two minutes
quests.why: You can disagree with someone and still respect them.
steps: Pick a topic with a grown-up: bedtime, screens, anything.
Two minutes each. Start with: I see it differently because.
No interrupting. Shake on it at the end.

quests.title: Hold a door, give up a seat or let someone go first, five times
quests.why: Small manners make the whole day smoother for everyone.
steps: Notice who is behind or near you.
Hold the door, give up your seat or let them go first.
Keep a tally on your fingers.

quests.title: Borrow something and give it back better than you found it
quests.why: Looking after other people's things is how you get to borrow again.
steps: Ask properly before you take it.
Look after it while it is yours.
Clean it or charge it, then give it back with thanks.

quests.title: Ask a grown-up about their day and listen to the whole answer
quests.why: Grown-ups have days too. Hardly anyone asks.
steps: Ask: what was the best bit of your day?
Listen, then ask one more question.
Tell them one thing you remember from it.

quests.title: Pick one thing you always moan about and make a plan to fix it
quests.why: Fixing a problem feels better than moaning about it.
steps: Write down the thing you moan about most.
Write three things you could do about it.
Do the first one today.

quests.title: Keep your voice kind when you are annoyed, all day
quests.why: A quiet voice gets heard better than a loud one.
steps: When annoyed, breathe out slowly first.
Drop your volume instead of raising it.
Say what is wrong in one sentence.

quests.title: Put your screen down when someone talks to you, every time
quests.why: Looking up tells people they matter more than the screen.
steps: When someone talks to you, put your screen face down.
Look up until they have finished.
Then pick it back up if you need to.

quests.title: Thank a teacher, coach or club leader in person
quests.why: They put in a lot for you. Most never hear it back.
steps: Pick one person who helps you outside home.
Tell them one thing they did that helped.
Say thank you and mean it.

quests.title: Choose one job and do it properly, no shortcuts
quests.why: Doing it right when nobody checks is what integrity means.
steps: Pick a job you usually rush.
Do every step properly, even the boring ones.
Say which step you normally skip.

quests.title: Tell a grown-up about a mistake you made this week
quests.why: Owning up takes courage. It also takes the weight off.
steps: Think of something small you got wrong and kept quiet.
Go and say it, plainly.
Say what you will do differently.

quests.title: Ask for what you want in a whole sentence, with a please
quests.why: Clear asking gets clear answers.
steps: Think of the whole sentence first.
Say it: please can I have, because.
Do it five times today.

quests.title: Tell a grown-up one thing you did today, start to finish
quests.why: Telling it in order helps people picture it.
steps: Pick one thing that happened.
Tell it in order: first, then, and at the end.
Ask if it made sense.

quests.title: Phone a family member and lead the whole chat
quests.why: Leading a conversation is a grown-up skill you can start now.
steps: Write three things to ask before you ring.
You say hello first and ask the questions.
You end the call politely.

quests.title: Ask three questions before you talk about yourself
quests.why: Curious people are the ones others want to talk to.
steps: In one conversation today, ask first.
Three real questions about them.
Notice what you learned.

quests.title: Say how you feel, and what made you feel it
quests.why: Naming the feeling and the reason helps people understand.
steps: Notice a feeling today, good or bad.
Say: I feel this, when that happens.
No blaming, just the feeling.

quests.title: With a grown-up beside you, ask a shop worker or librarian for help
quests.why: Asking someone who works there gets easier every time.
steps: Decide exactly what you need.
Your grown-up stays next to you. You do the talking.
Thank them and find it.

quests.title: Write a message with a greeting, one clear point and a sign-off
quests.why: A clear message gets a clear reply.
steps: Pick someone you know, with a grown-up’s OK. Hi, then their name.
One thing you want to say or ask.
Thanks, then your name. Send it.

quests.title: Practise saying no kindly: a grown-up asks three things, you decline each
quests.why: A kind, clear no is a skill you will use for life.
steps: A grown-up asks three things you would rather not do.
Say no thanks, with one reason.
Kind voice, no more than one sorry.

quests.title: Ask for help with something you have been stuck on
quests.why: Asking for help is what clever people do.
steps: Name the exact bit you are stuck on.
Ask someone: can you show me this part?
Try it yourself straight after.

quests.title: Repeat back what someone said before you answer, three times
quests.why: Checking you heard right stops a lot of arguments.
steps: Say: so you are saying, then their point.
Check you got it right.
Then give your answer.

quests.title: Sort out a disagreement with a friend by talking, not texting
quests.why: Some things are too important for a message.
steps: Pick a time to talk face to face or on a call.
Say your side, then ask theirs.
Agree one thing you will both do.

quests.title: Introduce yourself to someone new at a club, party or school
quests.why: Every friend was someone new once.
steps: Choose somewhere a grown-up knows you are, like a club or a party.
Say: hi, I am, what is your name?
Ask one question about them.

quests.title: Write a polite message to an adult outside the family, with a grown-up
quests.why: Writing to adults well opens a lot of doors.
steps: Agree who and why with a grown-up.
Greeting, purpose, thanks, name.
A grown-up reads it before it goes.

quests.title: Get dressed all by yourself, socks and all
quests.why: Getting dressed on your own is a very big deal.
steps: Lay your clothes out.
Pants, top, trousers, socks, in that order.
Show a grown-up when you are done.

quests.title: Brush your teeth for two whole minutes with no help
quests.why: Two minutes gets every tooth clean.
steps: Set a two-minute timer.
Top, bottom, front, back.
Rinse and put everything away.

quests.title: Pour your own drink without spilling
quests.why: Steady hands, full cup, dry table.
steps: Cup on the table, not in your hand.
Pour slowly, stop before the top.
Wipe up any drips yourself.

quests.title: Get ready for bed with no reminders, three nights
quests.why: A calm bedtime you run yourself feels grown-up.
steps: Pyjamas, teeth, toilet, book.
Nobody reminds you. Not once.
Three nights in a row.

quests.title: Pack your school bag the night before, three nights
quests.why: Mornings are easier when last night did the work.
steps: Check tomorrow: sport kit, reading book, letters.
Pack it and put it by the door.
Three school nights running.

quests.title: Make your own breakfast and clear up after
quests.why: Making your own breakfast is a proper grown-up start to the day.
steps: Choose something that needs no cooking, or just the toaster.
Make it and eat it.
Bowl in the sink or dishwasher, surface wiped.

quests.title: Remember all your own things for the day, no reminders
quests.why: Remembering your own stuff is a skill you will use forever.
steps: Make a list the night before.
Check it yourself in the morning.
A grown-up checks: no reminders needed.

quests.title: Set your own alarm and get up with it, three days
quests.why: Getting yourself up is the first job of the day.
steps: Set the alarm yourself.
Up within five minutes of it.
Three mornings running.

quests.title: Start your homework without being asked, three days
quests.why: Starting on your own is most of the battle.
steps: Pick your homework time.
Start before anyone mentions it.
Three days in a row.

quests.title: Fix something small that is broken
quests.why: Fixing things is cheaper and more satisfying than replacing them.
steps: Find something small: a loose screw, a flat tyre, a wobbly hook.
Work out what it needs and get the tool.
Fix it, with a grown-up checking any tools.

quests.title: Plan your whole week on one page: clubs, homework, kit
quests.why: A week on one page means nothing sneaks up on you.
steps: Seven days across the top.
Fill in every fixed thing and what it needs.
Stick it where you will see it.

quests.title: Try three fixes for a problem before asking anyone
quests.why: Most problems give way to the third try.
steps: Name the problem: homework, a gadget, a plan.
Try three different fixes and note each one.
Then ask, and say what you tried.

quests.title: Book an appointment or make an enquiry call yourself
quests.why: Phoning adults you do not know gets easier once you have done it.
steps: Agree the call with a grown-up, then write what you need and any dates.
Call, say who you are and what you want.
Check the details before you hang up.

quests.title: Do your own washing, start to finish, for a week
quests.why: Running your own washing is running your own life, a bit.
steps: Sort, wash, dry, fold, put away.
Every load of yours this week.
Nobody else touches it.

quests.title: Manage a small budget for a week and show the numbers
quests.why: Running a budget is the most useful maths there is.
steps: Agree an amount and what it must cover.
Track every spend.
Show what is left and what you would change.

quests.title: Drink water when you are thirsty, before anything sweet, all day
quests.why: Thirsty can feel like hungry or tired.
steps: Thirsty means water first.
A whole glass.
Then decide if you still want something sweet.

quests.title: Point to where a feeling lives in your body
quests.why: Feelings show up in your body first.
steps: Notice a feeling: excited, cross, nervous.
Tummy, chest, head, hands. Where is it?
Tell a grown-up the feeling and the place.

quests.title: Try a food you have said no to before, three bites
quests.why: Tastes change. Yours might have.
steps: Pick one food you usually refuse, that a grown-up says is fine for you.
Three real bites, chewed.
Say one word for the taste.

quests.title: Eat a rainbow: five colours of fruit or veg in a day
quests.why: Different colours do different good things for your body.
steps: Red, orange, yellow, green, purple.
Tick each colour as you eat it.
Count your colours at tea.

quests.title: Read the ingredients on a snack and say the first three
quests.why: The first three ingredients are what it is mostly made of.
steps: Find the ingredients list.
Read the first three out loud.
Say whether that surprised you.

quests.title: Make a snack from three whole ingredients
quests.why: Real food you put together yourself keeps you going longer.
steps: Three things not from a packet, that a grown-up is happy for you to use: fruit, yoghurt, oats, veg.
Put them together.
Eat it slowly.

quests.title: Swap one sugary snack for something that keeps you full
quests.why: Some snacks fill you up. Some just leave you wanting more.
steps: Spot the usual sugary snack moment.
Swap it for something with protein or fibre.
Notice how you feel an hour later.

quests.title: Name your tired signs out loud tonight, then start bedtime
quests.why: Your body tells you it is tired before you notice.
steps: Learn the signs: yawning, grumpy, rubbing eyes, silly.
Say them out loud as you spot them.
Two signs means bedtime starts, no argument.

quests.title: Notice how you feel one hour after a big sugary treat
quests.why: Learning how food changes your mood is useful for life.
steps: Have the treat. Note the time and your energy.
Set a timer for one hour.
Score your energy and mood out of five again. What changed?

quests.title: Plan and pack a lunch that keeps you going all afternoon
quests.why: A good lunch is fuel for the whole afternoon.
steps: Something filling, something fresh, water.
Pack it yourself.
At the end of the day, say whether you were hungry by three o’clock.

quests.title: Go a whole day with no fizzy drinks and say how it felt
quests.why: One day is enough to start noticing.
steps: Water, milk or squash only, all day.
Notice your energy and sleep.
One sentence on the difference.

quests.title: Spot a health claim on a packet and check whether it is true
quests.why: The front of a packet is an advert. The back is the truth.
steps: Find a packet that says natural, light or high in something.
Read the label on the back.
Say whether the front is telling the truth.

quests.title: Find out what protein, carbs and fats each do, and tell someone
quests.why: Knowing what food does lets you choose for yourself.
steps: Find out the job each one does: protein builds, carbs fuel, fats protect.
Find one food that is mostly each.
Explain it to a grown-up in under a minute.

quests.title: Log your energy morning, noon and night for three days
quests.why: Patterns only show up when you write things down.
steps: Energy out of five, three times a day.
Note what you ate and how you slept.
Find one pattern and say it.

quests.title: Put your own sun cream on, ears and back of neck too
quests.why: Sun cream only works where it goes.
steps: Use plenty: about a teaspoon for your face and neck alone.
Face, ears, neck, arms, legs.
Ask a grown-up to check your back.

quests.title: Set up the paddling pool or sprinkler, then clear it away
quests.why: The best bit of summer, and you get to run it.
steps: Set it up with a grown-up watching.
Play, with a grown-up watching the whole time.
Empty it, dry it and put it away.

quests.title: Make ice lollies from real fruit and freeze them
quests.why: Home-made lollies taste of actual fruit.
steps: Mash fruit with a splash of juice. A grown-up does any blending.
Pour into moulds or cups with sticks.
Wait. Then taste the first one.

quests.title: Plan and pack a picnic for the whole family
quests.why: Picnics taste better when someone thought of everything.
steps: Write the list: food, drinks, blanket, bin bag.
Pack it all yourself.
Lay it out when you get there.

quests.title: Sleep out in a tent in the garden
quests.why: The garden is a different place at night.
steps: Pitch it with a grown-up's OK, and help if you need it.
Torch, water, sleeping bag.
Stay out until morning.

quests.title: Keep a holiday scrapbook for two weeks
quests.why: Holidays go fast. A scrapbook keeps them.
steps: One page a day: a ticket, a drawing, a line.
Fourteen pages.
Read it to someone at the end.

quests.title: Learn to float on your back
quests.why: Floating is how you learn to trust the water.
steps: A grown-up in the water with you.
Ears in, tummy up, breathe slowly.
Float for ten seconds without being held.

quests.title: Paint a face on a pumpkin or a squash
quests.why: No carving needed. Paint does the talking.
steps: Pick a pumpkin or squash and some paints.
Plan the face on paper first.
Paint it and give it a name.

quests.title: Collect the brightest leaves and throw them up like confetti
quests.why: Bright leaves are only here for a few weeks. Use them.
steps: Grown-up along, coat on.
Gather a big armful of the brightest dry leaves you can find.
Count to three, throw them high, and spin while they fall.

quests.title: Build a bug hotel or a hedgehog hideout for winter
quests.why: Small creatures need somewhere to sleep through the cold.
steps: Pick a quiet corner outside with a grown-up.
Stack sticks, leaves, pine cones and bark with gaps.
Leave it alone so something can move in.

quests.title: Bake something with apples
quests.why: Apples are at their best right now.
steps: Pick a simple recipe: crumble, muffins, baked apples.
Weigh, peel and mix, with a grown-up for the oven.
Share it at pudding time.

quests.title: Make a leaf crown or a leaf picture
quests.why: Autumn gives you the colours for free.
steps: Collect leaves in as many colours as you can.
Stick them on a card strip or a sheet of paper.
Wear it or put it on the wall.

quests.title: Cut paper snowflakes and hang them in a window
quests.why: No two snowflakes are the same. Yours won't be either.
steps: Fold a square of paper into a triangle, then again.
Snip shapes out of the edges, with safe scissors.
Unfold and hang them up.

quests.title: Make a seed cake for the birds and hang it up
quests.why: Winter is a hard time for garden birds to find food.
steps: Mix seeds into soft lard or suet with a grown-up.
Press it into a pot or a cone with string.
Hang it and watch who comes.

quests.title: Write thank-you notes for three kind things people did for you this year
quests.why: The end of the year is a good time to say thank you.
steps: Think of three people who were kind to you this year.
Write or draw a note for each one.
Give them or post them with a grown-up.

quests.title: Frosty walk: find three frozen things
quests.why: Frost makes ordinary things sparkle.
steps: Coat, hat, gloves, grown-up.
Look for frost on leaves, webs, cars and puddles.
Find three and tell someone which was best.

quests.title: Make a card for someone who might be on their own this winter
quests.why: Winter can be lonely. A card says someone remembered.
steps: Think of someone with a grown-up: a neighbour, a relative.
Make a card with a warm message.
Post it or drop it round together.

quests.title: Warm drink, blanket, book, and the lights down low
quests.why: Cold dark evenings are made for this.
steps: A warm drink a grown-up makes for you.
A blanket and one good book.
Twenty minutes, lights down low.

quests.title: Make a paper windmill or kite and test it in the wind
quests.why: February has wind to spare. Put it to work.
steps: Make a windmill or kite from paper and a stick.
Take it outside with a grown-up on a windy day.
Find the spot where it spins or flies best.

quests.title: Plan a rainy-day indoor camp
quests.why: Rain outside, adventure inside.
steps: Pick the room and build a tent from blankets.
Plan camp food, a torch story and a game.
Run the camp for an hour, then pack it away.

quests.title: Write a friend a note saying why you are glad they are your friend
quests.why: Friends hardly ever tell each other this.
steps: Pick a friend.
Write one thing you like about them and one time they made you laugh.
Give it to them.

quests.title: Go on a walk and find five signs that spring is coming
quests.why: Spring starts quietly, if you look.
steps: Coat on, grown-up along.
Look for snowdrops, buds, birds building, lighter evenings.
Find five and tell someone.

quests.title: Set up an egg hunt with clues for someone else
quests.why: Hiding is even more fun than finding.
steps: Hide eggs, or paper eggs, around the house or garden.
Write or draw a clue for each one.
Watch someone else hunt.

quests.title: Plant sunflower seeds and measure them every week
quests.why: Plant them now and they could be taller than you by late summer.
steps: Plant seeds in small pots of soil.
Water them and put them somewhere sunny.
